Question: Two of the three sides of a triangle are \(20\) and \(15.\) Which of the following numbers is not a possible perimeter of the triangle?
Solution:
Let \(x\) be the third side. The triangle inequality requires it to be greater than the difference of the known sides and less than their sum:
\[
20-15<x<20+15,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad 5<x<35.
\]
The perimeter is \(P=35+x\), giving the strict range \(40<P<70\). The listed perimeters \(52,57,62,67\) correspond to third sides \(17,22,27,32\), all within the allowed range. A perimeter of \(72\) would require \(x=37\), which exceeds \(20+15\). Therefore the impossible perimeter is \(\boxed{72}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
